prompt: Write 5 short claim log entries by an auto insurance adjuster for a sideswipe while changing lanes claim. Injury: neck strain. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1413; do not mention it.)
text:
Entry 1: Claim opened following report of a sideswipe collision during a lane change. Insured vehicle contacted the claimant's vehicle on the driver's side rear quarter panel. Both drivers reported to be stopped at the scene and exchanging information. Claimant reports minor neck discomfort and was advised to seek medical evaluation. No attorney representation noted at this time.

Entry 2: Recorded statements obtained from both drivers. Insured states they checked mirrors and believed the adjacent lane was clear, but did not see the claimant's vehicle until contact. Claimant states they were already partially in the adjacent lane and maintaining speed. Photos of both vehicles uploaded to the file. Scene diagram requested from the responding officer's report.

Entry 3: Claimant contacted the office to report ongoing neck strain with stiffness and headaches. Claimant has scheduled an appointment with their primary care provider and expects an evaluation this week. Explained the medical payments coverage and the process for submitting treatment records. Claimant confirmed they are not represented by a lawyer and is handling the claim directly.

Entry 4: Medical records and initial treatment notes received from the claimant's provider. Diagnosis listed as cervical strain with recommendation for physical therapy and rest from strenuous activity. Reviewed vehicle damage estimate from the independent appraiser. Liability currently appears to favor the claimant based on the insured's admission of not confirming the lane was clear before moving over.

Entry 5: Physical therapy plan received and reviewed. Claimant reports improvement in range of motion but continued intermittent discomfort. Reserve adjusted to reflect the anticipated treatment course. Sent claimant a written summary of the claim status and the next steps needed to move the bodily injury portion forward. Follow-up call scheduled to confirm receipt of the summary.
